verses.text: Why doesn't the Almighty set times for judging? Why do those who know him never see those days?
Some people move boundary stones to steal land. They steal flocks and put them in their own pastures.
They drive away the orphan's donkey and take the widow's ox as a guarantee for a loan.
They push needy people off the road, and all the poor of the land have to hide.
Like wild donkeys in the desert, the poor go out to work, searching for food. The desert gives them food for their children.
They gather grain in other people's fields and pick the leftover grapes in the vineyards of the wicked.
They spend the night naked, with no clothes, with nothing to cover them in the cold.
They are soaked by mountain rains and hug the rocks because they have no shelter.
Some people snatch babies from their mothers' breasts. They take the babies of the poor as a guarantee for loans.
So the poor go around naked, without clothes. They carry bundles of grain but are still hungry.
They press olives between the walls of the rich and crush grapes in the winepresses, but they are still thirsty.
People groan in the crowded city, and the wounded cry out for help. Yet God does not notice that anything is wrong.
Some people rebel against the light. They do not know its ways or stay on its paths.
The murderer gets up at dawn and kills the poor and needy. At night he acts like a thief.
The person who sleeps with someone else's wife waits for evening. He thinks, 'No one will see me,' and he covers his face.
In the dark, robbers break into houses. During the day they shut themselves in. They want nothing to do with light.
For all of them, morning is like deep darkness. They are friends with the terrors of the dark.
They are like foam floating on the water. Their part of the land is cursed, and no one goes to their vineyards.
As heat and dry weather melt away the snow, so the grave takes away those who have sinned.
Their own mothers forget them. Worms feast on them. No one remembers them any more. So evil is broken like a tree.
They take advantage of women who have no children, and they do not help widows.
But God drags away the powerful by his strength. Even when they seem strong, they cannot be sure of their lives.
God may let them feel safe and secure, but his eyes are watching their ways.
They are great for a little while, and then they are gone. They are brought low and gathered up like everyone else. They are cut off like the heads of grain.
If this is not so, who can prove me a liar and show that my words are worth nothing?"
